title: On the complexity of the single-move labeled token routing problem
open: Is the single-move labeled token routing problem on a path solvable in linear time? Since the order of tokens never changes on a path, the set of sources left out can be chosen by dynamic programming along the path in polynomial time, but it is unknown whether the linear running time of the paper's theorem can be preserved.
status: The question is stated as open in the source (2026), from paper 2610.09084 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.09084). The polynomial-time dynamic programming approach on paths is known; the linear-time bound of the theorem's algorithm is not known to extend. Nicolas Bousquet was partly supported by ANR project ENEDISC (ANR-24-CE48-7768-01).
solved_when: (quantitative target) linear-time algorithm on paths, preserving the running time of the paper's theorem.
why: Resolving it would close the gap between the polynomial-time dynamic program on paths and the linear-time bound of the theorem, pinning down the true complexity of the problem in its simplest graph family.

title: The structure of irreducible cuspidal eta quotients
open: Does nonexistence of primitive irreducible holomorphic cuspidal eta quotients that are Fricke eigenforms extend to the remaining odd-level cases? Formally, for odd MATH, we conjecture that no primitive and irreducible holomorphic eta quotient exists which is a Fricke eigenform of level MATH.
status: Stated as open in the source, the paper arXiv:2610.10576 (2026).
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) of the conjecture: for every odd MATH, there exists no primitive and irreducible holomorphic eta quotient that is a Fricke eigenform of level MATH.
why: It would complete the structural classification of irreducible cuspidal eta quotients across all levels, pinning down exactly which levels admit such Fricke eigenforms.

title: Restrictions of the dot action representation — conjecture hposq
open: For a regular semisimple Hessenberg variety $(s,H)$ in the flag variety $G/B$ with Weyl group $W$, consider the dot action of $W$ on the cohomology $H^{*}(\mathcal{B}(s,H))$. If $W_J \subset W$ is a parabolic subgroup isomorphic to a symmetric group, is the restriction of the dot action on each even cohomology group $H^{2j}(\mathcal{B}(s,H))$ to $W_J$ a direct sum of permutation representations on coset spaces of parabolic subgroups of $W_J$?
status: The conjecture was stated as open in its source (2026), from paper arXiv:2610.04110; no resolution is recorded in the census.
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) is given that, for every regular semisimple Hessenberg variety in $G/B$ and every parabolic subgroup $W_J \subseteq W$ isomorphic to a symmetric group, each restricted representation $H^{2j}(\mathcal{B}(s,H))|_{W_J}$ for $j \geq 0$ decomposes as a direct sum of representations induced from permutation actions on coset spaces of parabolic subgroups of $W_J$.
why: It would give a uniform, combinatorial description of how the dot action representations of Weyl groups behave under restriction to symmetric-group parabolics, making the even cohomology of regular semisimple Hessenberg varieties explicitly computable in terms of coset actions.

title: Torsion of every finite order in the homology of graph braid groups
open: Does the higher homology of graph braid groups contain torsion of every finite order? Maci{a}\.zek and Sawicki's computations left open the question of the existence of torsion different than MATH in higher homologies.
status: Stated as open in the source (2026). In computations for complete graphs, complete bipartite graphs, and the Petersen family, Maci{a}\.zek and Sawicki found only copies of MATH, leaving the question open. Key work: https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.04305
solved_when: A graph is exhibited (or a proof given that none exists) for which the higher homology of its braid group contains torsion of orders other than MATH.
why: It would reveal whether graph braid group homology is structurally richer than current computations suggest, or confirm a strong rigidity of its torsion.

title: Torsion of every finite order in the homology of graph braid groups
open: Does the torsion assertion proved for at most three particles on parallel edges extend to four or more particles? Formally, the paper proves the assertion only up to three particles, and the case of four or more particles on parallel edges is left open in Question~.
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026), arXiv:2610.04305, where the same assertion is proven for parallel edges for at most three particles (Corollary~), leaving four or more particles open.
solved_when: The assertion is established (or refuted) for parallel edges with four or more particles.
why: It would complete the picture of torsion in the homology of graph braid groups for parallel edges beyond the three-particle barrier.

title: Domination and Total Domination in Johnson graphs
open: What are the domination number and the total domination number of the Johnson graph $J(n,k)$ when $k \ge 4$? In particular, is there an explicit formula for $\gamma(J(n,k))$ and $\gamma_t(J(n,k))$ in terms of $n$ and $k$, generalizing the known results for $k \in \{2,3\}$?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source (2026), from paper 2610.04675 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.04675), where the cases $k \in \{2,3\}$ are settled and the generalization to $k \ge 4$ is posed.
solved_when: Explicit formulas (in $n$ and $k$) for $\gamma(J(n,k))$ and $\gamma_t(J(n,k))$ are determined for all $k \ge 4$, or failing that, for an infinite family of $k$ values beyond $k \in \{2,3\}$.
why: These parameters quantify how small a family of $k$-subsets must be so that every other $k$-subset overlaps (or shares a neighbor with) one of them, a counting question with direct ties to covering designs; extending the formulas beyond $k \in \{2,3\}$ would complete the picture for one of the most classical families of association schemes.

title: Extension properties for partial permutations — problem prob:1.1
open: Does every finite tournament have the EPPA (also called the Hrushovski property)? In other words, given a finite tournament $A$, must there exist a finite tournament $B$ extending $A$ such that every partial automorphism of $A$ extends to an automorphism of $B$?
solved_when: A proof that for every finite tournament $A$ there is a finite tournament $B \supseteq A$ in which each partial automorphism of $A$ extends to an automorphism of $B$ (or a counterexample); the question is attributed to Herwig–Lascar.
why: It tests the reach of the Herwig–Lascar EPPA machinery beyond classes where extension properties are already known, with tournaments a basic structured case where the answer is unknown.

title: Extension properties for partial permutations
open: Does every finite tournament admit a finite extension with the extension property for partial automorphisms (EPPA)? In other words, given a finite tournament $A$, is there always a finite tournament $B$ extending $A$ such that every partial isomorphism of $A$ extends to a full isomorphism of $B$?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (arXiv:2610.04870, 2026); no partial results are recorded there.
solved_when: A construction (or impossibility proof) showing that every finite tournament $A$ has a finite tournament extension $B$ in which all partial isomorphisms of $A$ extend to automorphorphisms of $B$ — or a counterexample tournament for which no such finite $B$ exists.
why: Settling it would complete the picture of which finite structures satisfy the Hrushovski property, a key ingredient in model-theoretic and combinatorial arguments (such as those underlying extension properties for automorphism groups of countable structures).

title: Extension properties for partial permutations
open: Does the class of all finite tournaments have the extension property for partial automorphisms (EPPA, also known as the Hrushovski property)? Formally, can every finite tournament be embedded in a finite tournament in which every partial automorphism of the original extends to a full automorphism?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (arXiv:2610.04870, 2026), attributed there to Herwig–Lascar as a long-standing open problem. The same paper shows that MATH-weakly wandering problems all have odd-solutions and completely characterizes those without nilpotent-solutions.
solved_when: A proof that every finite tournament has EPPA, or a counterexample exhibiting a finite tournament whose partial automorphisms cannot all be extended within any finite tournament superstructure.
why: EPPA for finite tournaments is a long-standing open problem that motivated the research in the source paper; resolving it would settle a basic case of the Hrushovski property left open since Herwig–Lascar's work on extension properties.

title: Weak approximation for Campana points on projective spaces — campanaconj 1
open: Does weak approximation hold for Campana points on projective spaces, as predicted by the Campana conjecture?
status: Stated as open in the source, paper 2610.05032 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.05032), 2026.
solved_when: Weak approximation for Campana points on projective spaces is proved (or a counterexample is given), resolving the case raised in arXiv:2610.05032.
why: It would confirm the Campana conjecture's weak-approximation prediction in the simplest ambient setting, serving as a test case for the broader conjecture on rational points and Campana points.

title: On the generalized Sierpiński and Riesel numbers
open: What are the smallest Riesel and Sierpiński numbers? Despite numerous efforts and extensive computer calculations, determining them exactly remains unresolved.
status: Stated as an open problem in the source paper (arXiv:2610.05149, 2026).
solved_when: The smallest Riesel number and the smallest Sierpiński number are each explicitly identified, with proof that no smaller candidates exist.
why: These values are fundamental constants of number theory, and pinning them down would settle a long-computed but unproved boundary between the known candidates and the true minima.

title: Quantum n-coloring is undecidable for every n $\ge$ 3
open: Is quantum graph coloring undecidable in general? More precisely, is it the case that for every non-bipartite graph $H$, the quantum $H$-coloring problem is undecidable?
solved_when: A proof (or refutation) is given of the conjecture that quantum $H$-coloring is undecidable for every non-bipartite graph $H$.
why: A resolution would establish the exact decidability frontier for quantum coloring problems, separating the bipartite (decidable) case from all non-bipartite targets.

title: Quantum n-coloring is undecidable for every n $\ge$ 3
open: What is the computational complexity of quantum MATH-coloring for a general fixed graph MATH?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (2026), arXiv:2610.05280.
solved_when: The complexity of quantum MATH-coloring is characterized for every fixed graph MATH (e.g., by placing it in a complexity class or showing undecidability/completeness).
why: It would complete our understanding of when quantum coloring problems become computationally intractable, extending the known undecidability results to the general fixed-graph setting.

title: A Proof of the Linear Hadwiger Conjecture — conjecture c:ListHadwiger
open: Does a linear form of Hadwiger's conjecture hold for list coloring? That is, is there a positive constant $C$ such that for every integer $t \geq 1$, every graph with no $K_{t}$ minor is $Ct$-list colorable?
status: The conjecture is stated as open in the source paper (2026), arXiv:2610.05291; no partial results are given in the record.
solved_when: A positive constant $C$ is exhibited (with proof) such that every graph with no $K_{t}$ minor admits a list coloring from lists of size $Ct$, for every integer $t \geq 1$.
why: It would establish a linear list-coloring analogue of Hadwiger's conjecture, showing list-chromatic number is within a constant factor of the clique-minor obstruction.

title: Amicable numbers
open: Over a billion amicable pairs are known, yet no method is known that could prove infinitely many exist. Can we prove that the number of amicable pairs is infinite?
status: Over a billion amicable pairs are known. The problem is stated as open in the source paper (arXiv:2610.05661), 2026.
solved_when: A proof is given that there exist infinitely many pairs of distinct positive integers $(m, n)$ with $\sigma(m) = \sigma(n) = m + n$, where $\sigma$ is the sum-of-divisors function.
why: Amicable pairs sit between perfect numbers and general aliquot cycles; an infinitude proof would likely introduce techniques applicable to the wider landscape of divisor-sum equations, where even perfect numbers' infinitude remains out of reach.

title: Symmetries on vector parking functions via bounded lattice paths
open: Is there a direct combinatorial explanation for the symmetries on vector parking functions arising here? The known argument merely composes the involutions MATH and MATH, so the question is to find a construction that exhibits the symmetry without passing through that composition.
status: The problem is stated as open in the source, paper 2610.05665 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.05665), which notes that the symmetries follow from composing the involutions MATH and MATH and poses a direct combinatorial explanation as an interesting open direction.
solved_when: A direct combinatorial object or bijection is constructed that explains the symmetries on vector parking functions via bounded lattice paths, without simply composing the involutions MATH and MATH.
why: A direct bijection would reveal the structural reason behind the symmetry, giving a combinatorial proof usable for refinement, statistics, and extension to related families, whereas the composition of involutions obscures the underlying structure.

title: On three conjectures of Kimberling concerning the array $\lfloor k\var — conjecture conj:disjoint
open: For every $n \geq 1$, are the rows $R_{2n-1}$ and $R_{2n}$ of the array $\lfloor k\varphi \rfloor$ disjoint? Formally, the conjecture asserts that $R_{2n-1} \cap R_{2n} = \emptyset$ for all $n \geq 1$.
status: Stated as open in the source (2026), arXiv:2610.05776 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.05776).
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) is given of the statement that $R_{2n-1} \cap R_{2n} = \emptyset$ for every $n \geq 1$.
why: It settles one of the three conjectures of Kimberling concerning the array $\lfloor k\varphi \rfloor$, resolving a stated open question from the source paper.

title: On three conjectures of Kimberling concerning the array $\lfloor k\var — conjecture conj:strong
open: Is it true that for every $n \geq 1$, if the numbers in rows $2n-1$ and $2n$ of Kimberling's array $\lfloor k\varphi \rfloor$ are arranged together in increasing order and each number is replaced by its position in this ordering, then the two resulting rows coincide with rows $1$ and $2$?
status: Stated as open in the source, arXiv:2610.05776 (2026), where it appears as one of three conjectures of Kimberling concerning the array $\lfloor k\varphi \rfloor$.
solved_when: The above property is proved for every $n \geq 1$, or a counterexample $n$ is exhibited.
why: The conjecture concerns the structure of rows of the Kimberling array; resolving it would clarify the self-similar ordering behavior of the array $\lfloor k\varphi \rfloor$.

title: On three conjectures of Kimberling concerning the array $\lfloor k\var — conjecture conj:occ
open: Does every positive integer occur infinitely often in the sequence $(a(N))_{N\ge 1}$? Equivalently, is it true that for each $m \ge 1$ the set $\{N : a(N) = m\}$ is infinite?
status: The conjecture is stated as open in the source (2026), the paper arXiv:2610.05776 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.05776).
solved_when: A proof (or disproof, via an integer occurring only finitely many times) of the infinitude of occurrences of every positive integer in $(a(N))_{N\ge 1}$.
why: It resolves one of three Kimberling conjectures about the array $\lfloor k\varphi \rfloor$, settling the occurrence structure of the sequence and completing part of the program set out in the source paper.

title: On three conjectures of Kimberling concerning the array $\lfloor k\var
open: For every value $v \ge 2$, must the smallest index $N$ at which the Kimberling array $\lfloor k\varphi \rfloor$ attains the value $v$ be exactly the Lucas number $L_{4v-5}$? This is the fourth of Kimberling's three conjectures — conjecture 4 as stated in the source paper.
status: Stated as open in the source, the paper arXiv:2610.05776 (2026).
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) that for every $v \ge 2$, the least $N$ with $a(N) = v$ equals $L_{4v-5}$, where $L_n$ denotes the Lucas sequence.
why: Resolving it would settle the last of Kimberling's conjectures about the structure of the array $\lfloor k\varphi \rfloor$, pinning down exactly where each value first appears.

title: When the BSD Real Period Remembers Elliptic Curves over $\mathbb{Q}$ — unnumberedquestion 1
open: Can an elliptic curve over $\mathbb{Q}$ be recovered, up to isomorphism, from the invariants that appear in the Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture — in particular, the real period together with the other BSD data? More precisely, one asks whether these invariants determine the curve's $\mathbb{Q}$-isomorphism class.
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) that the BSD invariants — including the real period — determine an elliptic curve over $\mathbb{Q}$ up to $\mathbb{Q}$-isomorphism.
why: A positive answer would give a new arithmetic fingerprint for elliptic curves over $\mathbb{Q}$, showing the analytic BSD data alone rigidly determines the curve; a negative answer would reveal distinct curves sharing all BSD invariants, obstructing reconstruction from analytic data.

title: A counterexample to the circuit-cocircuit intersection conjecture — conjecture conj:oxley
open: Does the circuit-cocircuit intersection conjecture (conjecture conj:oxley) hold in matroid theory, or can it fail? Formally, the question is whether the conjecture attributed to Oxley survives as stated, given a claimed counterexample.
solved_when: A definitive determination that the conjecture holds (a proof) or fails (a verified counterexample) is established.

title: On rigidity properties of unit-distance graphs
open: Does there exist a generically globally rigid penny graph or marble graph that is penny- (respectively marble-) rigid but not globally penny- (respectively marble-) rigid? In other words, can rigidity and global rigidity genuinely diverge at the level of individual graphs in these contact-graph settings?
status: The question is stated as open in the source (2026), the paper arXiv:2610.06246.
solved_when: An explicit penny graph or marble graph is exhibited that is generically globally rigid and penny- (respectively marble-) rigid yet not globally penny- (respectively marble-) rigid; alternatively, a proof that no such graph exists.
why: It clarifies whether the relationship between rigidity and global rigidity, known at the general level, holds graph by graph for penny and marble graphs — a gap between the two notions would show global rigidity demands strictly more than rigidity in these geometric settings.

title: Theta Series with Half-integral Characteristics
open: Does the vanishing of the odd trace imply that every odd-characteristic theta series in the same degree vanishes? In other words, can one pass from a trace condition on theta series with half-integral characteristics to pointwise vanishing of each odd-characteristic series?
solved_when: A proof (or a counterexample) is given showing, in any fixed degree, whether vanishing of the odd trace forces every odd-characteristic theta series to vanish.
why: It would settle a basic structural question about theta series with half-integral characteristics, clarifying how trace-level information controls the individual series.

title: Ehrhart Properties under Operations on Lattice Polytopes
open: Which operations on lattice polytopes preserve desirable Ehrhart-theoretic properties such as unimodality of the h\*-polynomial? The motivating question in this direction — whether the h\*-polynomial of every lattice polytope with the integer decomposition property (IDP) is unimodal — has recently been resolved negatively, so the challenge is to understand what additional structure or which operations restore such behavior.
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (arXiv:2610.06338, 2026). The record notes that the well-known motivating problem — unimodality of the h\*-polynomial for IDP lattice polytopes — was recently resolved negatively.
solved_when: A characterization (or a proof/counterexample framework) is given of the operations on lattice polytopes that preserve unimodality of the h\*-polynomial, together with an analysis of the IDP case in light of its recent negative resolution.
why: Since IDP alone does not force unimodality of h\*-polynomials, identifying which constructions and operations do would delineate the true boundary of Ehrhart-theoretic regularity and give usable sufficient conditions in combinatorics of polytopes.

title: Ehrhart Properties under Operations on Lattice Polytopes
open: Does every smooth lattice polytope admit a regular unimodular triangulation? More formally, is Oda's conjecture true — that every smooth lattice polytope can be triangulated into unimodular simplices without moving its vertices?
status: The question is stated as open in the source (2026), the paper arXiv:2610.06338.
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) that every smooth lattice polytope has a unimodular triangulation, as asked in Oda's smoothness problem.
why: A positive answer would give smooth polytopes a clean combinatorial structure — unimodular triangulations yield explicit formulas for Ehrhart polynomials and toric data — and would settle a long-standing basic question about how smoothness constrains lattice geometry.

title: Geometric Realizations with Strong Self-Duality Part II: Diameter Grap
open: What is the largest number of edges an $n$-vertex stress-free diameter framework in $\mathbb{R}^d$ can have?
status: The question is stated as open in the source (2026), the paper https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.06340.
solved_when: A sharp upper bound (or exact formula) for the maximal number of edges in such a framework is established, with matching constructions.
why: It calibrates how dense a geometric graph can remain while stress-free, a basic extremal question for rigidity-type frameworks.

title: Geometric Realizations with Strong Self-Duality Part II: Diameter Grap
open: If $X \subset \mathbb{R}^4$ is a finite set of points in general position, meaning no five lie on a hyperplane, must the diameter framework of $X$ be stress-free? Equivalently, does the graph joining pairs of points at diameter distance always admit a geometric realization carrying no nonzero self-stress?
status: The question is stated as open in the source, arXiv:2610.06340 (2026).
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) is given for the stress-freeness of the diameter framework of every finite point set in $\mathbb{R}^4$ in general position, i.e. with no five points on a common hyperplane.
why: This settles the four-dimensional case of the question of when diameter graphs admit self-stress-free realizations, a basic structural question in the rigidity theory of diameter frameworks.

title: Geometric Realizations with Strong Self-Duality Part II: Diameter Grap
open: Is it true that every simple non-bipartite quadrangulation map $Q$ of the projective plane can be realized as the diameter graph of an extremal set $X \subset \mathbb{R}^3$, in such a way that the automorphism group $Aut(Q)$ acts as a group of isometries on $X$?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (arXiv:2610.06340, stated as open in 2026); no partial results are recorded in the census.
solved_when: For an arbitrary simple non-bipartite quadrangulation map $Q$ of the projective plane, an extremal set $X \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ is exhibited whose diameter quadrangulation is exactly $Q$ and on which $Aut(Q)$ acts by isometries.
why: It would complete the geometric realization program for this class of projective-plane quadrangulations while preserving all combinatorial symmetries as geometric ones, showing the symmetry of $Q$ is faithfully reflected in its realization.

title: Geometric Realizations with Strong Self-Duality Part II: Diameter Grap — problem prob:densesym
open: If a finite group $H$ occurs as the symmetry group of a Reuleaux polyhedron, must the Reuleaux polyhedra whose symmetry group contains $H$ be dense in the family of all constant-width bodies with symmetry group $H$?
status: Stated as open in the source (2026), arXiv:2610.06340 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.06340); no partial results are recorded.
solved_when: For every Reuleaux-polyhedron symmetry group $H$, the set of Reuleaux polyhedra with symmetry group containing $H$ is dense (in the natural topology on bodies) in the set of constant-width bodies with symmetry group $H$.
why: It would show that the highly symmetric Reuleaux polyhedra are not isolated curiosities but approximate every symmetric constant-width body, extending strong self-duality from discrete realizations to the continuous setting.

title: Geometric Realizations with Strong Self-Duality Part II: Diameter Grap
open: Is every stress-free diameter framework in $\mathbb{R}^d$ colorable with $d+1$ colors? Equivalently, does the graph underlying such a framework admit a proper $(d+1)$-coloring?
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) that for every $d$, every stress-free diameter framework in $\mathbb{R}^d$ is $(d+1)$-colorable.
why: It would give a geometric route to bounding chromatic numbers of a natural class of frameworks arising from diameter graphs, connecting rigidity theory to graph coloring.

title: Geometric Realizations with Strong Self-Duality Part II: Diameter Grap
open: Suppose $C$ is a smooth strictly convex body in $\mathbb{R}^3$. Which graphs arise as tangency graphs of families of pairwise intersecting translates of $C$?
solved_when: A characterization is given of exactly which graphs can be realized as tangency graphs of a family of pairwise intersecting translates of any smooth strictly convex body $C$ in $\mathbb{R}^3$.
why: It would extend the classical theory of intersection and tangency graphs (such as coin graphs in the plane) to a natural three-dimensional convex-geometric setting, delimiting the combinatorial structure forced by convexity and smoothness.

title: Degeneracy loci and unlikely intersections in abelian schemes
open: Does Pink's conjecture on unlikely intersections hold in full generality for abelian schemes? That is, can the known special cases be extended to the general statement of {conj:Pink}?
status: Pink's conjecture remains open in general, though several cases are known; the problem is stated as open in the source paper arXiv:2610.06518 (2026).
solved_when: A proof (or refutation) of Pink's conjecture in the general setting of abelian schemes is established, beyond the several special cases already known.
why: The general case is the outstanding gap in the unlikely-intersections program for abelian schemes; settling it would complete the theory that the known special cases only partially cover.

title: Counting Cylinders on Z-covers of Genus 2 Square-tiled Surfaces
open: Is the count of families of saddle connections, or of maximal cylinders of simple closed geodesics of bounded length, always asymptotically quadratic in the bound — for all translation surfaces? More precisely: does the asymptotic growth for counting saddle-connection families or maximal cylinders of simple closed geodesics of length at most the given bound remain quadratic across every translation surface?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (arXiv:2610.06609), from which it is extracted verbatim as an open problem; no progress toward a solution is recorded in the census.
solved_when: A proof (or disproof, via an explicit translation surface) that for all translation surfaces the number of such families of saddle connections or maximal cylinders of simple closed geodesics of length at most the bound grows quadratically asymptotically.
why: Establishing a universal quadratic law would settle a basic growth question about translation surfaces, giving a uniform asymptotic that cylinder-counting results on specific classes of surfaces could build on; a counterexample would reveal surfaces whose geodesic structure deviates from the expected geometry.

title: The linear independence of $1$, $ζ(3)$, and $ζ(4)$
open: Is $1$, $ζ(3)$, and $ζ(4)$ linearly independent over the rationals — in particular, does no nontrivial rational linear combination of these three numbers vanish? More precisely, the record notes that even the irrationality of the quantity in question remains open.
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) of the linear independence of $1$, $ζ(3)$, and $ζ(4)$ over $\mathbb{Q}$; no quantitative targets are stated in the record, so the natural criterion applies.
why: It would advance the study of arithmetic relations among zeta values, where rational linear relations beyond Euler's identities remain poorly understood.

title: Cubic vertices in minimal braces — conjecture conj:HLZ2026+
open: Does every minimal brace with at least six vertices contain a $3$-line? More precisely, is every such brace guaranteed to have a vertex of degree three?
status: The conjecture is stated as open in the source, arXiv paper 2610.06933 (2026), from which it was extracted.
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) is given that every minimal brace with at least six vertices has a $3$-line.
why: It would establish a basic structural property of minimal braces, constraining how small such objects can be; a counterexample would reveal minimal braces that are structurally richer than expected.

title: Equilibria of Inverse-Square Repulsion on the Line Are Arithmetic Prog
open: The source record contains no actual problem statement for this entry — only boilerplate acknowledgments and provenance text — so no well-formed open question can be given.
status: Stated as open in the source (2026); the problem comes from paper 2610.06944 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.06944).
solved_when: No success criterion is stated in the record; the natural criterion would be a proof or disproof that equilibria of inverse-square repulsion on the line form arithmetic progressions.
why: No motivation is given in the record beyond extraction from the source paper's full text.

title: The compress-with-another threshold of Szykuła's Figure 3 family
open: What is the exact compress-with-another threshold for the corrected Figure 3 family of automata from Szykuła's survey of open problems? That is, precisely how many applications of a "compress-with-another" operation are needed for this family, stated as an exact pair-distance question in the pair automaton?
status: Stated as open in the source (2026), paper 2610.07044 (Qichao Wang, "The compress-with-another threshold of Szykuła's Figure 3 family"), which gives a self-contained pair-automaton proof of the exact threshold for the corrected Figure 3 family.
solved_when: The exact compress-with-another threshold of the corrected Figure 3 family is determined, with a self-contained proof (e.g., via the pair automaton) giving the exact value for every member of the family.
why: An exact threshold resolves one of the open problems posed in Szykuła's survey and sharpens our understanding of compressibility in synchronizing automata beyond bounds.

title: The One-Power Erdős Conjecture for Primes $p \equiv 7 \pmod{36}$ — conjecture conj:onepower
open: Can every prime $p$ be written as $p = 2^a + m$, where $a \geq 0$ is an integer and $m$ is a squarefree positive integer?
status: Stated as open in the source (2026), the paper 2610.07214 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.07214); no resolution is recorded.
solved_when: A proof (or disproof, via an explicit counterexample prime) that every prime $p$ admits such a representation $p = 2^a + m$ with $a \geq 0$ an integer and $m$ squarefree and positive.
why: It would resolve the "one-power" variant of Erdős's conjecture covered in paper 2610.07214, giving a structural decomposition of primes into a power of two plus a squarefree part.

title: Near-factorizations in association schemes
open: Are there near-factorizations of non-cyclic abelian groups? More precisely, does a non-cyclic abelian group admit a near-factorization, beyond the known cyclic-group constructions?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source (arXiv:2610.07394, 2026), which notes that no near-factorizations of non-cyclic abelian groups are currently known.
solved_when: Either an explicit near-factorization of some non-cyclic abelian group is exhibited, or such near-factorizations are proved impossible for all non-cyclic abelian groups.
why: It would extend the theory of near-factorizations beyond the cyclic setting, where the known constructions currently reside.

title: Near-factorizations in association schemes — quest 6
open: For which subgroups $H$ of $GL(d,p)$ is the Schurian association scheme arising from the primitive group $\mathbb{F}_{p^d} H$ algebraically isomorphic to the Hamming scheme $H(d,p)$?
status: Stated as open in the source (2026), the paper arXiv:2610.07394.
solved_when: A complete characterization is given of the subgroups $H \leq GL(d,p)$ for which the Schurian scheme of the primitive group $\mathbb{F}_{p^d} H$ is algebraically isomorphic to the Hamming scheme $H(d,p)$.
why: It identifies exactly when a linear-group construction reproduces the classical Hamming scheme, clarifying which primitive groups yield combinatorial structure indistinguishable from Hamming space.

title: Pattern avoidance in alternating sign rectangles I: Extended avoidance
open: Based on computer experiments, is there a closed-form formula for the number of extendably MATH-avoiding alternating sign rectangles?
status: The conjecture was stated as open in the source paper (arXiv:2610.07442), based on computer experiments.
solved_when: A closed-form formula for the number of extendably MATH-avoiding ASRs is conjectured and proved, matching the computer-experimental data.
why: A closed form would convert experimental enumeration data into a provable structural result about extended pattern avoidance in alternating sign rectangles.

title: Lifting ethereal Bianchi modular forms
open: Does every ethereal mod $p$ Bianchi modular form over a norm-Euclidean imaginary quadratic field $K$ admit a lift to characteristic $0$ at higher level?
solved_when: A proof (or construction) that every ethereal mod $p$ Bianchi modular form over a norm-Euclidean imaginary quadratic field $K$ admits a characteristic $0$ lift at higher level.
why: Establishing such lifts would extend the lifting theory of Bianchi modular forms to the ethereal case, a setting where no characteristic $0$ lift is currently guaranteed.

title: A proof of the Erdős--Gallai cycle decomposition conjecture
open: Is the Erdős–Gallai cycle decomposition conjecture true? The problem is the second open problem stated in the source paper, and it concerns whether graphs can be decomposed into cycles in the manner the conjecture asserts.
status: Stated as open in the source (2026), arXiv:2610.07840.
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) of the Erdős–Gallai cycle decomposition conjecture as stated in the source paper is given.
why: The conjecture was included by Erdős in several of his collections of open problems, and resolving it settles a long-standing question in graph decomposition.

title: A proof of the Erdős--Gallai cycle decomposition conjecture
open: Does every graph admit a decomposition into cycles and edges whose total number is at most the number of vertices with odd degree, as the Erdős–Gallai conjecture on cycle decompositions asserts? The companion Gallai conjecture on path decompositions remains equally unresolved.
status: Both conjectures are stated as open in the source paper (arXiv:2610.07840, 2026); no further state of the art is recorded.
solved_when: A proof (or refutation) of the Erdős–Gallai cycle decomposition conjecture is given, together with, ideally, the analogous resolution of Gallai's path decomposition conjecture.
why: These are foundational decomposition conjectures that pin down how efficiently a graph's edge set can be partitioned into cycles and paths, and resolving them would settle a basic structural question in graph theory.

title: Semisimplicity, purity and Mumford-Tate conjecture for hyper-Kähler va
open: Does the Mumford–Tate conjecture hold for hyper-Kähler varieties? Originally formulated for abelian varieties, the conjecture remains open in general, even in that case; see the source paper and the references therein for an overview.
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (arXiv:2610.07890, 2026); the Mumford–Tate conjecture remains open in general, even for abelian varieties.
solved_when: The Mumford–Tate conjecture (semisimplicity and purity of the relevant Galois/motivic structure included) is proved for hyper-Kähler varieties in general, or at least the record's stated scope is settled by a proof or counterexample.
why: Settling it would extend the arithmetic theory of Hodge and Tate classes from abelian varieties to hyper-Kähler varieties, determining the extent to which l-adic Galois images capture the Hodge structure.

title: Semisimplicity, purity and Mumford-Tate conjecture for hyper-Kähler va — conj Conjecture:WMC
open: Let $X$ be a smooth proper scheme over $K$ — which structural properties of its cohomology (such as semisimplicity, purity, or the Mumford–Tate conjecture) hold for hyper-Kähler varieties in this setting?
status: Stated as open in the source, arXiv:2610.07890 (2026).
solved_when: The conjecture stated in the source paper (Conjecture:WMC on semisimplicity, purity and the Mumford–Tate conjecture for hyper-Kähler varieties) is proven or disproven for smooth proper schemes over $K$.
why: A resolution would establish the Mumford–Tate behavior of hyper-Kähler varieties, a key bridge between Hodge theory and étale cohomology in this class.

title: Unimodality of Forest Independence Polynomials — conjecture conj:993
open: For a forest — or even just a tree — is the sequence counting independent sets of each size unimodal, meaning it never decreases and then increases in alternating fashion? Formally, if a_k is the number of independent vertex sets of size k, must a_0 ≤ a_1 ≤ … up to some point and then be nonincreasing thereafter?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (arXiv:2610.07943, 2026); no partial resolutions are recorded.
solved_when: A proof (or disproof with an explicit counterexample forest) that the independence polynomial of every tree — or, more generally, every forest — has unimodal coefficient sequence.
why: Unimodality of independence polynomials is a basic structural question in combinatorics; establishing it for the natural class of forests would settle a conjecture left open in the source literature and clarify which graph classes admit unimodal independence sequences.

title: Diagonal Specht ideals and their varieties — conjecture conj:hook
open: If a partition is a hook, is the associated diagonal Specht ideal $I_{R_{m,n}}$ radical for all $n$ and $m$? Formally: for every hook partition, the diagonal Specht ideal $I_{R_{m,n}}$ is radical for all choices of $n$ and $m$.
status: Stated as open in the source (2026), arXiv:2610.07955.
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) that for every hook partition, $I_{R_{m,n}}$ is radical for all $n$ and $m$.
why: Radiality of these ideals controls the geometry of diagonal Specht varieties, so a proof would establish that the corresponding varieties decompose without embedded components.

title: Perfect state transfer on mixed graphs: complete classes and transfer — question prob:classification
open: Which finite subsets of $R/\mathbb{Z}$ containing zero can arise as the sets of normalized transfer times of complete perfect-state-transfer classes at nonstationary periodic vertices in connected mixed graphs? More precisely, a characterization is sought of exactly those finite sets, always containing zero, that occur this way.
solved_when: A complete characterization is given of the finite subsets of $R/\mathbb{Z}$ containing zero that occur as normalized transfer time sets of complete PST classes at nonstationary periodic vertices in connected mixed graphs.
why: Such a characterization would settle which transfer-time spectra are realizable in mixed-graph quantum walk dynamics, delimiting the possible periodic behavior beyond what plain graphs allow.

title: Perfect state transfer on mixed graphs: complete classes and transfer — question prob:global
open: Can a connected globally periodic mixed graph have a perfect state transfer class of arbitrarily large size? Formally, is there a family of such graphs in which the set of vertices exhibiting perfect state transfer to a fixed vertex grows without bound?
status: Stated as open in the source, the paper arXiv:2610.08333 (2026).
solved_when: A construction of connected globally periodic mixed graphs with perfect state transfer classes whose size is unbounded (or a proof that some fixed bound always holds).
why: It would determine whether perfect state transfer in mixed graphs is a genuinely rich phenomenon or confined to small, rigid classes, guiding which graph families are viable for transfer-based quantum walk protocols.

title: Special Loci in the Moduli of Curves
open: (de Jong) Are there infinitely many primes $p$ such that there is a 1-parameter family of supersingular quintic surfaces of characteristic $p$?
status: Stated as open in the source (2026), the paper arXiv:2610.08382; no partial results are recorded in the census.
solved_when: An infinite set of primes $p$ is exhibited, each admitting a 1-parameter family of supersingular quintic surfaces in characteristic $p$ (or a proof that only finitely many such primes exist).
why: It would reveal how supersingularity distributes across the moduli of high-degree surfaces as the characteristic varies, a basic unknown about arithmetic degeneration beyond the classical cases of lower degree.

title: Cayley graph diameters for fixed cycle types are eventually quasipolyn
open: Is there a general formula for the diameters of the Cayley graphs arising from permutations of a fixed cycle type that works for all cycle structures at once? The source establishes exact quasipolynomial-type expressions in several families — for example, for permutations supported on exactly k−1 letters, giving a piecewise answer depending on parity, and for permutations all of whose cycles have length at most k, giving cases such as (n−1)/3 plus a quasipolynomial correction for k = 5, n/4 plus a correction for k = 6, (n−1)/4 for k = 7, and (n−1)/5 plus a correction for k = 8 — but a uniform formula valid for all cycle types remains unclear.
status: The problem is stated as open in the source (2026), paper 2610.08385 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.08385), which proves exact quasipolynomial answers for several specific families but leaves the general formula for all cycle types unclear.
solved_when: A single general formula for the Cayley graph diameter is given that covers arbitrary fixed cycle types, reproducing the known case-by-case quasipolynomial expressions (including the parity-dependent formula for permutations supported on exactly k−1 letters and the k = 5, 6, 7, 8 cases for cycles of bounded length) as instances.
why: A uniform formula would turn a growing collection of ad hoc diameter computations into a structural theorem about how cycle type controls the geometry of these Cayley graphs, and would settle the diameter question for any new cycle type without further case analysis.

title: On the structure of certain valued fields II — question question:motivation
open: Fix a prime $p$ and a positive integer $e$. How large must the residue rings be before they determine a finitely ramified complete discretely valued field of mixed characteristic $(0,p)$ with ramification index $e$? Formally, what is the lifting number $N_p(e)$, the smallest $n$ such that any two such fields $K_1$ and $K_2$ are isomorphic whenever two residue rings of length $n$ are isomorphic?
status: Stated as open in the source (2026); see https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.08395.
solved_when: An explicit value (or sharp bounds) for the smallest $n$ is determined for each prime $p$ and ramification index $e$.
why: A quantitative lifting number would bound how much finite-level residue data suffices to recover a valued field, sharpening local structure theorems for finitely ramified mixed-characteristic fields.

title: On the maximum degree and order of $K_t$-minor-free graphs with positi — prob prob:top
open: For every $t \ge 5$, is there a function $g(t)$ such that any connected graph with no topological $K_t$ minor, maximum degree at most $t-1$, and positive Lin–Lu–Yau curvature on every edge has maximum degree bounded by $g(t)$? Equivalently, must such a graph have order at most $g(t)^{2g(t)(g(t)-1)}$?
solved_when: A function $g(t)$ is exhibited, with proof that every connected graph $G$ with no topological $K_t$ minor, $\Delta(G) \le t-1$, and positive Lin–Lu–Yau curvature on every edge satisfies $\Delta(G) \le g(t)$ and hence $|V(G)| \le g(t)^{2g(t)(g(t)-1)}$.
why: It would show that positive Lin–Lu–Yau curvature together with a topological-minor exclusion forces graph order to be bounded in terms of $t$ alone, giving a curvature-based analogue of boundedness results for minor-closed classes.

title: Positivity for graph Laurent phenomenon algebras
open: For every directed graph without loops or multiple edges, is each cluster variable of the associated graph Laurent phenomenon algebra a Laurent polynomial with nonnegative coefficients in the variables of any cluster?
status: The conjecture is stated as open in the source paper (arXiv:2610.08914, 2026). No partial results are recorded in the census.
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) of the positivity statement: for every loopless directed graph without multiple edges, every cluster variable of its graph LP algebra, expanded in the variables of any cluster, is a Laurent polynomial with nonnegative coefficients.
why: Positivity of this kind is the analogue of the classical cluster algebra positivity theorem; establishing it would show graph LP algebras retain the good structural behavior that underpins applications like laurent phenomenon-based constructions and positivity-preserving mutations.

title: Distinguishing graphs with simple spectrum by homomorphism counts
open: Does every graph class that is complete for homomorphism-distinguishing power on graphs with simple spectrum necessarily contain graphs with arbitrarily large clique minors? In other words, is unbounded treewidth (via clique minors) unavoidable for any class that captures all simple-spectrum graphs in this sense?
status: Stated as open in the source, arXiv:2610.09042 (2026).
solved_when: A proof (or refutation) is given that every class complete on simple spectrum contains graphs with arbitrarily large clique minors.
why: It would clarify whether homomorphism-count completeness on simple-spectrum graphs forces a structural condition like unbounded clique minors, constraining which graph classes can serve as complete distinguishing families.

title: On the complexity of the single-move labeled token routing problem
open: What is the complexity of monotone reconfiguration of unit disks in the plane when any disk may fill any target and a disk may initially overlap a target — the geometric counterpart of the all-matching case of single-move labeled token routing? In particular, can such reconfigurations always be achieved, and if so at what computational cost?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (arXiv:2610.09084, 2026), attributed to Abrahamsen and Halperin's list of ten open problems in geometric robotics; no progress beyond this statement is recorded.
solved_when: A resolution of the open problem posed by Abrahamsen and Halperin in their list of ten open problems in geometric robotics, namely a determination of whether monotone reconfiguration of unit disks in the plane under all-matching (any disk may fill any target, initial overlap of targets allowed) is always feasible, together with its complexity classification.
why: It settles the natural geometric analogue of the all-matching single-move labeled token routing case, extending the complexity picture from the combinatorial setting to continuous geometric motion planning.

title: On the complexity of the single-move labeled token routing problem
open: Is the single-move labeled token routing problem still NP-hard on grid graphs in the unique-matching case when each token may move at most twice? In other words, we do not know whether the theorem establishing hardness in the more restrictive movement setting extends to this at-most-two-moves setting.
solved_when: The question is settled by either a proof that the unique-matching case remains NP-hard on grid graphs when each token may move at most twice, or a proof (e.g., a polynomial-time algorithm) that it does not.
why: It pins down the exact role of the movement budget in the hardness of single-move token routing on grids, sharpening the boundary between tractable and intractable variants of the problem.

title: On graphs whose powers are well-covered — prob 1
open: Which simple graphs have the property that every graph power is well-covered? Formally, classify all simple graphs $G$ such that $G^d$ is well-covered for every $d \geq 1$.
status: The problem is stated as open in the source (2026), the paper arXiv:2610.09300.
solved_when: A complete characterization (structural classification) of all simple graphs $G$ for which $G^d$ is well-covered for every $d \geq 1$, together with a proof of its correctness.
why: A classification would reveal how well-coveredness — the property that all maximal independent sets have equal size — behaves under taking powers, connecting distance-based graph constructions to a classical covering invariant.

title: On graphs whose powers are well-covered — quest 2
open: If every power $G^d$ of a simple connected graph $G$ is well-covered for all $d \geq 1$, must $G$ have diameter at most 3? And if $\mathrm{diam}(G) = 3$, are there only finitely many such graphs with no true twins?
status: Stated as open in the source (2026), arXiv:2610.09300 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.09300); no partial results recorded.
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) that $G^d$ well-covered for all $d \geq 1$ forces $\mathrm{diam}(G) \leq 3$, together with a determination of whether the diameter-3 graphs without true twins satisfying this condition form a finite family.
why: It would characterize, via diameter alone, which connected graphs have all powers well-covered, giving a complete structural picture of this class.

title: A linear bound for a connectivity partition in graphs
open: Is there a function $g$ such that, for every positive integer $k$, every strongly $g(k)$-connected digraph can be partitioned into two sets, each inducing a strongly $k$-connected digraph? In other words, can sufficiently high strong connectivity always be split into two highly strongly connected parts?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source (2026), the paper arXiv:2610.09365.
solved_when: An explicit function $g$ is given (or its existence proved) such that for every positive integer $k$, every strongly $g(k)$-connected digraph admits a partition into two sets each inducing a strongly $k$-connected digraph.
why: It would establish that strong connectivity can be partitioned in digraphs, a basic structural question with no known bound.

title: Non-uniqueness of optimal $1$-embeddings on surfaces up to weak equiva
open: Does there exist an optimal $1$-embedded graph on the projective plane or the Klein bottle that admits two weakly inequivalent optimal $1$-embeddings? Formally, the question asks for a single graph and two optimal embeddings into one of these surfaces that are not related by the notion of weak equivalence considered in the source paper.
solved_when: An explicit optimal $1$-embedded graph on the projective plane or the Klein bottle is produced together with two weakly inequivalent optimal $1$-embeddings; alternatively, a proof that no such graph exists on either surface.
why: It would settle whether optimal $1$-embeddings on these two nonorientable surfaces are unique up to weak equivalence, completing the uniqueness picture left open by the source paper.

title: Characterizing chordal $\llcorner$-EPG graphs via admissible clique tr
open: Chordal $\llcorner$-EPG graphs have now been fully characterized structurally, but can they be recognized efficiently — does there exist a polynomial-time algorithm that decides whether a given chordal graph admits an edge intersection representation by paths on a grid using only $\llcorner$-shaped paths?
status: Stated as open in the source (arXiv:2610.09443, 2026). The paper fully characterizes chordal $\llcorner$-EPG graphs but leaves the polynomial-time recognition algorithm open.
solved_when: A polynomial-time recognition algorithm for chordal $\llcorner$-EPG graphs is given, closing the second part of the question posed in the source paper.
why: The structural characterization without an accompanying recognition algorithm leaves the class unusable in algorithmic practice; a polynomial-time algorithm would complete the picture, making chordal $\llcorner$-EPG graphs a fully tractable graph class.

title: Coloring Monomial Cayley Graphs: The One-Parameter Case
open: How many colors are needed to color monomial Cayley graphs in the one-parameter case? We conjecture that three colors suffice for every algebraic noninteger direction parameter, and that four colors suffice for every direction parameter.
solved_when: The conjecture is resolved: a proof that every algebraic noninteger direction parameter admits a 3-coloring, together with a proof that every direction parameter admits a 4-coloring.
why: It pins down the exact chromatic behavior of the one-parameter family of monomial Cayley graphs, closing the main coloring question left open for this family.

title: Graph Sensitivity of Cartesian Products with Matched Bridges — problem prob:excess
open: Is $f_2(Q_9)$ equal to $3$ or to $4$? More broadly, how sharply can the factor threshold in Theorem (i) be pinned down, and what are the values of $f_t$ in the remaining finite-factor cases for hypercubes, Cartesian products of trees with perfect matchings, and Cartesian products of even-order paths?
status: Stated as open in the source (2026), arXiv:2610.09483.
solved_when: The exact value of $f_2(Q_9)$ (either $3$ or $4$) is determined, the factor threshold in Theorem (i) is sharpened, and $f_t$ is determined in all remaining finite-factor cases for hypercubes, Cartesian products of trees with perfect matchings, and Cartesian products of even-order paths.
why: Resolving these cases would complete the finite-factor picture for these graph families, closing the explicit gaps the source paper leaves open rather than leaving them as isolated undecided values.

title: Reconstruction of slices of cubes
open: Are hyperplane sections of a product of simplices class reconstructible? That is, can such a section be recovered, up to the natural equivalence of the theory, from knowledge only of its class?
status: The question is stated as open in the source paper, from arXiv:2610.09939 (2026); no progress beyond the statement is recorded here.
solved_when: A proof (or refutation) that every hyperplane section of a product of simplices is class reconstructible, as stated as open in the source paper (arXiv:2610.09939).
why: It would extend reconstruction results to an important family of polytopes arising as slices of cubes/products of simplices, clarifying how much of such a section is determined by its class data.

title: Reconstruction of slices of cubes
open: It would be interesting to determine whether the vertex-edge graph still determines the combinatorial type.
status: stated as open in source (2026)

title: Asymptotic connectivity, hamiltonicity and toughness — conjecture conj HCG
open: Is every finite connected Cayley graph on at least three vertices hamiltonian?
status: Stated as open in the source (2026), the paper arXiv:2610.09992 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.09992); no further results are recorded in the census.
solved_when: A proof (or counterexample) is given for the statement that every finite connected Cayley graph on at least 3 vertices contains a Hamilton cycle.
why: It would settle a long-standing structural question about how symmetry forces Hamiltonicity, showing the Cayley condition alone suffices — a counterexample would fundamentally reshape the search for hamiltonicity criteria.

title: Asymptotic connectivity, hamiltonicity and toughness — problem prob snake
open: Is there a universal constant $R$ such that the hypercube $Q_n$ contains an $R$-dense induced cycle for every $n>1$? In other words, does every vertex of $Q_n$ lie within distance $R$ of some single induced cycle, with $R$ independent of $n$?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (arXiv:2610.09992, 2026); no partial results are recorded in the census.
solved_when: An explicit universal constant $R$ is exhibited such that $Q_n$ has an $R$-dense induced cycle for every $n>1$, together with a proof; equivalently, a proof that no such constant exists would resolve the question negatively.
why: A positive answer would show that a single sparse induced structure — a cycle — can uniformly approximate all of the hypercube, yielding strong simultaneous control over asymptotic connectivity, hamiltonicity, and toughness-type properties of $Q_n$.

title: The local dynamical structure of $Δ^*$ sets via a new Furstenberg fami
open: Is the countability assumption in the thick-conclusion lemma ({lemma_thick_conclusion}) genuinely necessary, or can it be dropped? In other words, we do not know whether the stated dynamical conclusion for $Δ^*$ sets holds without imposing countability where the lemma currently requires it.
status: The problem is stated as open in the source (2026), the paper arXiv:2610.10416, from which the countability assumption in {lemma_thick_conclusion} originates.
solved_when: A proof or counterexample is given showing that the countability hypothesis in {lemma_thick_conclusion} can be removed, or that it cannot — i.e., the lemma's conclusion fails for some non-countable instance.
why: It determines whether the local dynamical structure established for $Δ^*$ sets via the new Furstenberg family holds in full generality or only under the auxiliary countability restriction.

title: The structure of irreducible cuspidal eta quotients — conj 00:00AM
open: For odd $n$, can there exist a primitive, irreducible holomorphic eta quotient of level $2^n$ that is a Fricke eigenform? The conjecture asserts that no such eta quotient exists.
status: Stated as open in the source (2026), the paper arXiv:2610.10576.
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) of the assertion that for every odd $n$ there is no primitive and irreducible holomorphic eta quotient that is a Fricke eigenform of level $2^n$.
why: It would clarify the structural constraints on cuspidal eta quotients at pure powers of two, ruling out an entire class of Fricke eigenforms at these levels.

title: Obstructions to $k$-colouring $H$-free graphs — conjecture conj:P4UellP1
open: Fix an integer $k \ge 5$. Is it true that there are only finitely many $k$-vertex-critical $H$-free graphs if and only if $H$ is an induced subgraph of $P_4 + \ell P_1$ for some $\ell \ge 0$?
status: Stated as open in the source (2026), the paper arXiv:2610.10737.
solved_when: A proof (or refutation) of the stated equivalence for every fixed $k \ge 5$: finiteness of the family of $k$-vertex-critical $H$-free graphs holds exactly when $H$ is an induced subgraph of $P_4 + \ell P_1$ for some $\ell \ge 0$.
why: It would give a complete structural characterization of which forbidden induced subgraphs $H$ make $k$-colourability of $H$-free graphs finitely certified by critical graphs, yielding decidability-style finiteness results for the associated colouring problems.

title: Obstructions to $k$-colouring $H$-free graphs — openproblem prob:hereditary
open: For which values of $k>3$ and which hereditary classes of graphs $H$ are there only finitely many $k$-vertex-critical graphs in $H$?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source (2026), the paper arXiv:2610.10737. No partial results are recorded in the census entry.
solved_when: A characterization is given of the pairs $(k, H)$ with $k>3$ and $H$ a hereditary class for which the set of $k$-vertex-critical graphs in $H$ is finite, together with a proof that all other pairs admit infinitely many such graphs.
why: Finiteness of the $k$-vertex-critical obstructions is what turns membership in a hereditary class into a certifiable, finitely-testable property relative to $k$-colourability, so the answer delineates exactly where such finite obstruction sets exist.

title: Obstructions to $k$-colouring $H$-free graphs
open: For which graphs $H$ are there only finitely many $k$-vertex-critical $(2P_3,H)$-free graphs for all $k \geq 1$? That is, which forbiddance pairs force the family of vertex-critical obstructions to $k$-colouring to be finite in every chromatic number?
status: The problem is stated as open in the source paper (arXiv:2610.10737, 2026); no characterization or partial results are recorded here.
solved_when: A complete characterization of the graphs $H$ such that, for every $k \geq 1$, only finitely many $k$-vertex-critical $(2P_3,H)$-free graphs exist.
why: A characterization would delimit exactly when the finitely-many-obstructions phenomenon holds, enabling explicit descriptions of all critical graphs and, with them, polynomial-time recognition of $k$-colourability for the corresponding hereditary classes.

title: Obstructions to $k$-colouring $H$-free graphs — openproblem prob:infinitethenfinite
open: For a fixed $k \geq 4$, can one find a finite list of pairwise nonisomorphic graphs $H_1, H_2, \ldots, H_n$, each with $\chi(H_i) < k$, such that the class of $(H_1, H_2, \ldots, H_n)$-free graphs contains, for some $m \geq k$, infinitely many $m$-vertex-critical graphs and infinitely many $(m+1)$-chromatic graphs, yet only finitely many $(m+1)$-vertex-critical graphs?
status: Stated as open in the source, the paper arXiv:2610.10737 (2026).
solved_when: An explicit finite family of nonisomorphic graphs $H_1, \ldots, H_n$ with $\chi(H_i) < k$ for all $i \in \{1, 2, \ldots, n\}$ (for some fixed $k \geq 4$) is produced whose induced-subgraph-free class contains infinitely many $m$-vertex-critical graphs and infinitely many $(m+1)$-chromatic graphs, but only finitely many $(m+1)$-vertex-critical graphs, for some $m \geq k$.
why: Such a family would separate the infinitude of vertex-critical graphs from one chromatic level to the next within a finitely described hereditary class, exposing a new obstruction to extending finiteness-of-obstructions results for $k$-colouring $H$-free graphs.

title: Equidistribution of number theoretic point sets in the torus and the s
open: Does there exist a badly approximable system of vectors in the sense considered here? Littlewood's conjecture asserts that no such system exists.
status: Stated as open in the source (2026), arXiv:2610.10881 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.10881).
solved_when: A proof or disproof of the existence of a badly approximable system of vectors as defined in the source; equivalently, a resolution of Littlewood's conjecture, which states such a system does not exist.
why: A resolution would settle Littlewood's conjecture, a central question in simultaneous Diophantine approximation concerning the interplay between badly approximable systems and equidistribution of number theoretic point sets in the torus.

title: Distinct flattened partitions avoiding a pattern of length four
open: Is the number of distinct flattened partitions of $[n]$ avoiding the pattern 2341 equal to sequence A307786 evaluated at $n-1$, for every $n \geq 1$? In symbols, does $p_n(2341) = A307786(n-1)$ hold for all $n \geq 1$?
status: Stated as open in the source (2026), arXiv:2610.11271 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11271); no proof is known.
solved_when: A proof (or disproof with counterexample) of the identity $p_n(2341) = A307786(n-1)$ for all $n \geq 1$.
why: It would settle one of the conjectured enumerations for length-four pattern avoidance among distinct flattened partitions, linking that counting sequence to a known OEIS entry.

title: An asymptotic bound for the Bermond--Thomassen Conjecture
open: Is the Bermond–Thomassen Conjecture true in full generality — that is, for every digraph with minimum out-degree at least 2k, must the vertex set partition into k disjoint directed cycles? The source states that the exact conjecture for general digraphs remains open.
status: The problem is stated as open in the source, arXiv:2610.11517 (2026), with no partial results recorded in the census.
solved_when: A proof (or disproof) of the exact Bermond–Thomassen Conjecture for general digraphs; no quantitative targets beyond the conjecture itself are given in the record.
why: A full resolution would settle a foundational question on cycle structure in digraphs; without it, only special or approximate cases can be claimed.

title: An asymptotic bound for the Bermond--Thomassen Conjecture
open: Does every digraph with minimum out-degree at least $2k-1$ contain at least $k$ vertex-disjoint directed cycles? Formally, is there a constant $C$ such that every digraph of minimum out-degree at least $Ck$ admits $k$ vertex-disjoint directed cycles, yielding an asymptotic bound for the Bermond--Thomassen Conjecture?
solved_when: A proof (or construction target: a proof) that every digraph with minimum out-degree at least $Ck$ contains $k$ vertex-disjoint directed cycles for some absolute constant $C$ and all positive integers $k$.
why: It would give the first asymptotic resolution of the Bermond--Thomassen Conjecture, settling the qualitative truth of the conjecture up to a constant factor in the out-degree threshold.

title: An asymptotic bound for the Bermond--Thomassen Conjecture
open: Does every digraph with sufficiently large minimum out-degree contain many vertex-disjoint directed cycles? Formally, the Bermond--Thomassen Conjecture asserts that every digraph with minimum out-degree at least MATH contains MATH disjoint directed cycles, and it remains open in general.

why: It is a foundational question on how out-degree forces cycle structure in digraphs; resolving it would settle a long-standing conjecture about packing disjoint directed cycles in general digraphs.

title: Noncrossing combinatorics of quasi-Coxeter elements — conjecture conj:EL

why: EL-shellability yields a well-behaved Möbius-function and homology structure for these intervals, extending noncrossing-combinatorics tools beyond the classical Coxeter elements.

title: Arithmetic Progressions in Midpoint Colourings
open: Suppose the numbers $1, 2, \ldots, N$ are coloured with $k$ colours in such a way that whenever two distinct numbers $x$ and $y$ have a midpoint belonging to a fixed set $R \subseteq [N]$ (i.e., $x + y = 2r$ for some $r \in R$), then $x$ and $y$ must receive different colours. For fixed $k$, how large can the set $R$ be as a function of $N$?
status: Stated as open in the source (2026), the paper arXiv:2610.11847; no bounds or partial results are recorded in the census.
solved_when: An answer, for each fixed positive integer $k$, giving the maximum possible size of $R \subseteq [N]$ (up to explicit constants or asymptotics in $N$) under the stated midpoint-difference colouring constraint.
why: It quantifies how restrictive midpoint-based colouring constraints are, directly bounding the size of a "midpoint set" compatible with a $k$-colouring, a natural Ramsey-type parameter for additive structure.

title: Pythagorean pairs in boxes of prime powers

status: Stated as open in the source, the paper at https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11965 (2026); the finite two-colour problem is settled, and the corresponding question for three or more colours remains open.

why: It completes the finite colouring picture for Pythagorean pairs over boxes of prime powers, extending beyond the settled two-colour case.

title: Constructing pathological symmetric abstract rigidity matroids
open: For each $d \geq 2$, do there exist infinitely many positive integers $n$ for which some symmetric abstract $d$-dimensional rigidity matroid on $K_n$ is not contained in any abstract $d$-rigidity matroid family?
status: Stated as open in the source, arXiv paper 2610.12036 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12036), recorded in 2026; no progress beyond the statement is given.
solved_when: For every $d \geq 2$, an infinite set of positive integers $n$ is exhibited, each carrying a symmetric abstract $d$-dimensional rigidity matroid on $K_n$ not contained in any abstract $d$-rigidity matroid family.
why: It would produce symmetric abstract rigidity matroids that provably escape the axiomatic framework of rigidity matroid families, showing symmetry can force genuinely pathological behavior.
